body.p: These remarks are responsive to the Office action dated September 19, 2024. Prior to entry of this response, claims 1, 3-13, and 15-19 were pending in the application. By way of this response, claims 1, 4-7, and 15 are amended, and claims 20 and 21 are added. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the application and allowance of the
pending claims.
Claims 1, 3-6, 8-13, and 15-19 rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 on the asserted basis that the claimed invention is directed to non-statutory subject matter.
Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection but has amended claims 1 and 15 to further highlight the patent-eligible subject matter. Amended claim 1 recites:
A system for determining a cognitive state of a user of a vehicle to control one or more functions of the vehicle, the system being implemented by one
or more controllers, the system comprising:
one or more inputs for receiving user data from a plurality of
associated user monitoring devices for each monitoring at least one respective attribute of the user of the vehicle, the user data being indicative
of the plurality of respective attributes;
one or more electronic processors configured to execute a plurality
of inference modules and an inference fusion module, wherein:

the plurality of inference modules is each arranged to receive user data from one or more of the user monitoring devices, and to each determine a respective inference of a cognitive state of the user based at least in part on the received user data, wherein each of the plurality of inference modules is arranged to output user state data indicative of the
determined inference of the cognitive state of the user; and

the inference fusion module is arranged to receive the user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, to determine an inference of an aggregated cognitive state of the user and to output cognitive state data indicative of the aggregated cognitive state for controlling the one or more functions of the vehicle based thereon, the inference fusion module being further configured to determine, in dependence on the received user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, likelihood data indicative of a current likelihood of the user being in one or more cognitive states, and determine the inference of the aggregated cognitive state based at least in part on whether the likelihood data exceeds a threshold for that
cognitive state for longer than a minimum period of time; and
an output configured to output control data for controlling the one
of more functions of the vehicle, the control data generated based on the
cognitive state data.
Support for the amendments to claim 1 may be found at least at previously presented claim 7 and paragraphs [0018], [0030], [0076], [0110], [0112], [0113], and [0134] of Applicant's specification.

On pages 5 and 6 of the Office action, the Office asserts that certain elements of claim 1, such as the plurality of inference modules arranged "to each determine a respective inference of a cognitive state of the user based at least in part on the received user data, wherein each of the plurality of inference modules is arranged to output user state data indicative of the determined inference of the cognitive state of the user" and "the inference fusion module is arranged to receive the user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, to determine an inference of an aggregated cognitive state of the user and to output cognitive state data indicative of the aggregated cognitive state for controlling the one or more functions of the vehicle based thereon," constitute a mental process and thus claim 1 recites an abstract idea. The Office further states that the alleged abstract idea is not incorporated into a practical application and that the additional claim elements do not provide significantly more than the abstract idea. See pages 6 and 7 of the Office action.

As an initial matter, Applicant notes that the Office states on page 8 of the Office action that "claim 7 has a controlling step that overcomes 101 Alice rejection rational[e]." Claim 1 has been amended herein to include subject matter from claim 7.

While Applicant disagrees that claim 1 includes limitations that recite an abstract idea, the alleged abstract idea is incorporated into a practical application because claim 1, as amended herein, includes specific features that were specifically configured to achieve an improved technological result and provide improvements to a technical field. For example, amended claim 1 recites "an output configured to output control data for controlling the one of more functions of the vehicle, the control data generated based on the cognitive state data." As explained in Applicant's specification, by controlling one or more functions of the vehicle based on an aggregated cognitive state of a user (e.g., as conveyed via the control data, which is generated based on the cognitive state data), the need for the user to manually control functionality of the vehicle may be reduced, which may be particularly advantageous for autonomous vehicles (e.g., due to the user not being in a position to control each function of the vehicle or not being prepared to control each function of the

vehicle). Further, when the user is in charge of operating the vehicle, reducing manual control of certain functions of the vehicle may allow the user to concentrate on driving the vehicle. Further still, by controlling one or more functions of the vehicle based on the aggregated cognitive state of the user, the operation of the vehicle may be improved by more efficiently responding to user needs and preferences, which may reduce unnecessary operation of the vehicle's HVAC system, for example.

In this way, the configuration of amended claim 1 provides an improvement to the functioning of a technical field (e.g., vehicle operation). Further, the inclusion of elements in addition to the alleged abstract idea (e.g., "an output configured to output control data for controlling the one of more functions of the vehicle, the control data generated based on the cognitive state data") impose meaningful limits on the alleged abstract idea. Further still, the elements of amended claim 1, in combination, perform functions that are not generic computer functions.

Additionally, amended claim 1 recites something significantly more than just the alleged abstract idea, as the elements of amended claim 1 are not generic processes, such as merely instructions to apply the alleged abstract idea, but rather the claim includes specific implementation steps, such as "the inference fusion module being further configured to determine, in dependence on the received user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, likelihood data indicative of a current likelihood of the user being in one or more cognitive states, and determine the inference of the aggregated cognitive state based at least in part on whether the likelihood data exceeds a threshold for that cognitive state for longer than a minimum period of time." Specifically, amended claim 1 is not merely directed to a simple judgement as alleged by the Office, but instead includes specific details for how the aggregated cognitive state of the user may be determined. In this manner, amended claim 1 does not seek to tie up the alleged abstract idea. In particular, the determination of likelihood data and temporal threshold analysis via the inference fusion module represents an improvement to how computer systems can process and analyze cognitive state data. As explained at paragraph [0113] of Applicant's specification, this approach helps filter out noise and false positives in a way that would not be possible through mental processes.
As enumerated in MPEP § 2106.05, limitations that the courts have found to qualify as "significantly more" when recited in a claim with a judicial exception include:

improvements to the functioning of a computer; improvements to any other technology or technical field; applying the judicial exception with, or by use of, a particular machine; effecting a transformation or reduction of a particular article to a different state or thing; adding a specific limitation other than what is well-understood, routine, conventional activity in the field, or adding unconventional steps that confine the claim to a particular useful application; or other meaningful limitations beyond generally linking the use of the judicial exception to a particular technological environment. In the present case, amended claim 1 provides an improvement to a technology or technical field (e.g., vehicle performance) and adds specific limitations other than what is well-understood, routine, and conventional in the field (e.g., "the inference fusion module being further configured to determine, in dependence on the received user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, likelihood data indicative of a current likelihood of the user being in one or more cognitive states, and determine the inference of the aggregated cognitive state based at least in part on whether the likelihood data exceeds a threshold for that cognitive state for longer than a minimum period of time").

Thus, amended claim 1 is not directed to an abstract idea, and, even if it was, the alleged abstract idea is integrated into a practical application and the elements of amended claim 1 provide significantly more than the alleged abstract idea. Accordingly, the rejection of claim 1 and all claims depending therefrom should be withdrawn. Similar points apply to claim 15, and thus the rejection of claim 15 should likewise be withdrawn.
Claims 1-9 and 12-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)/102(a)(2) as being anticipated by United Kingdom Reference No. GB 2528083 (Popham et al., hereinafter Popham).
Claims 10, 11, and 19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Popham in view of U.S. Patent No. 9,977,593 (Ricci).

Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections. The cited references fail to disclose each and every element of amended claim 1. The Office relies solely on Popham in the rejection of claim 1. However, Popham fails to disclose at least the amended claim 1

element of "the inference fusion module is arranged to receive the user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, to determine an inference of an aggregated cognitive state of the user and to output cognitive state data indicative of the aggregated cognitive state for controlling the one or more functions of the vehicle based thereon, the inference fusion module being further configured to determine, in dependence on the received user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, likelihood data indicative of a current likelihood of the user being in one or more cognitive states, and determine the inference of the aggregated cognitive state based at least in part on whether the likelihood data exceeds a threshold for that cognitive state for longer than a minimum period of time."

On page 9 of the Office action, the Office cites page 8, lines 6-22 and page 9, lines 4-10 of Popham as allegedly disclosing an inference fusion module arranged to receive the user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, to determine an inference of an aggregated cognitive state of the user and to output cognitive state data indicative of the aggregated cognitive state for controlling the one or more functions of the vehicle based thereon. Therein, Popham discloses that flags may be returned upon input of parameters and that processing may be done on the flags to determine a mood of a user, such that if "most" of the flags are associated with a particular mood (e.g., tired), the system may infer that the user emotion state is that particular mood. Whether or not Popham discloses that combinations of scaled factors and probabilities can be more accurately used to assess mood, Popham fails to disclose that the inference fusion module is "further configured to determine, in dependence on the received user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, likelihood data indicative of a current likelihood of the user being in one or more cognitive states, and determine the inference of the aggregated cognitive state based at least in part on whether the likelihood data exceeds a threshold for that cognitive state for longer than a minimum period of time." In this way, Popham has no recognition that the user emotion state can be determined at least in part on whether any of the mood flags (or scaled factors or probabilities) have exceeded a threshold for longer than a minimum period of time. As such, Popham fails to achieve the benefits of the claimed configuration, namely filtering out noise and false positives to ensure a more accurate determination of the user cognitive state and, in turn, more accurate and precise control of the one or more functions of the vehicle.

While Applicant does not acquiesce to the correctness of the rejection, Applicant notes that in the rejection of claim 1, the Office cites page 3, line 25 through page 4, line 5 of Popham as allegedly disclosing "an active time monitor arranged to receive an indication of the active state from the threshold monitor and to determine, based at least in part on a temporal threshold value, the inference of the cognitive state of the user." The cited section of Popham discloses that values of a plurality of types of parameters indicative of a user emotion state may be received, that the parameters may be a time or location, and that a parameter may be obtained from a device configured to record a condition parameter, wherein the device may record the time, a time elapsed since a previous record or event, or a climate parameter. Whether or not "a time elapsed" discloses determining an inference of a cognitive state of a user based at least in part on a temporal threshold value (which, for the record, Applicant disputes), the cited time elapsed since a previous record or event does not disclose that the inference fusion module is "further configured to determine, in dependence on the received user state data from each of the plurality of inference modules, likelihood data indicative of a current likelihood of the user being in one or more cognitive states, and determine the inference of the aggregated cognitive state based at least in part on whether the likelihood data exceeds a threshold for that cognitive state for longer than a minimum period of time," as required by amended claim 1.

Thus, the rejections of claim 1 and all claims depending therefrom should be withdrawn. The remaining cited reference (Ricci) fails to cure the deficiencies of Popham. As claim 15 has been amended similarly to claim 1, claim 15 is allowable over the cited references for at least the reasons discussed above with respect to claim 1, and, as such, the rejection of claim 15 should be withdrawn.

New claims 20 and 21 have been added. Support for claim 20 may be found at least at previously presented claim 1. Support for claim 21 may be found at least at paragraphs [0106] and [0107] of Applicant's specification. As claims 20 and 21 each depend from claim 1, they are allowable over the cited references for at least the reasons discussed above with respect to claim 1.

Applicant believes that this application is now in condition for allowance, in view of the above amendments and remarks. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner issue a Notice of Allowability covering the pending claims.
